title: keel
description: State, load shed, trips and open circuits for every breaker, decisions, refusals and errors for every rate limiter, and inbound admission for every overload limiter, published with breaker.Register, ratelimit.Register, retry.Register, fallback.Register and overload.Register.

panels.title: Circuit open, fraction of instances
panels.description: Per dependency: the share of instances whose circuit is open. Red across the row is the dependency being down; a thin sliver is one pod (often CPU-throttled). Inline equivalent of the breaker:open_fraction recording rule.

targets.expr:
sum by (dependency) (go_breaker_state{dependency=~"$dependency", state="open"})
  /
count by (dependency) (go_breaker_state{dependency=~"$dependency", state="closed"})

panels.title: Open now
panels.description: Current fraction of instances open, per dependency.

targets.expr:
sum by (dependency) (go_breaker_state{dependency=~"$dependency", state="open"})
  /
count by (dependency) (go_breaker_state{dependency=~"$dependency", state="closed"})

panels.title: Load shed, share of calls refused
panels.description: The user-facing symptom: calls that never ran because the circuit was open, the probe budget was exhausted, or the bulkhead was full.

panels.title: Trips
panels.description: Transitions to open per interval, summed across instances. A comb pattern is flapping: the backend is half-recovering, or IsFailure counts healthy answers as failures.

panels.title: In flight vs limit
panels.description: Bulkhead headroom. Solid lines are calls in flight, dashed lines the current cap (absent when unlimited). A solid line pinned to its dashed line is a slow backend filling the bulkhead; under the adaptive bulkhead the dashed line saws up and down. A dashed line climbing one step per call right after a recovery is the recovery ramp (go_breaker_ramping == 1), not a problem.

panels.title: Error rate
panels.description: Worst instance's share of calls in the trailing WithErrorRate window that failed, per dependency. A line climbing to the configured threshold precedes a trip by the rate rule; a flat zero is a healthy window or a breaker without the rule. The gauge follows Stats, so on an idle instance it holds its last value until something inspects the breaker.

panels.title: Open circuits
panels.description: One row per open breaker. 'Next probe in' counts down to the next admitted probe; negative means the breaker is idle with its deadline passed and will go half-open on the next call (lazy expiry, not a fault). 'Consecutive trips' is how deep into exponential backoff it is.

panels.title: Circuit state per instance
panels.description: One row per breaker instance. Use the dependency variable to narrow it; with a large fleet this is the drill-down view, not the overview.

panels.title: Decisions per second, by result
panels.description: Allowed, limited and error decisions per limiter. Stacked: the total height is demand, the limited band is what the quota is turning away.

panels.title: Refused share
panels.description: Limited decisions as a share of all decisions, per limiter. Inbound: how hard clients are being throttled. Outbound: how far over quota you are.

panels.title: Limiter errors
panels.description: Decisions that could not be made: a distributed limiter whose Redis is unreachable or misbehaving. With the default fail-open middleware this is the only signal that limits are not being enforced.

panels.title: Keys tracked
panels.description: Per-key records currently kept by each local limiter; bounded by WithMaxKeys. Not reported for Redis limiters, whose records live in Redis.

panels.title: Retries per call
panels.description: Attempts beyond the first, per call. Above one half means most calls are retried: the dependency is degraded, or WithRetryIf retries answers. Inline equivalent of the retry:retries_per_call recording rule.

panels.title: Calls per second, by result
panels.description: Stacked: the total height is demand; exhausted is the user-facing failure, aborted a non-retryable error, budget a retry the budget refused, which during an incident is the budget working. The dashed series is hedges started per second: attempts WithHedge added because the ones in flight were slow. Compare it with go_retry_hedge_wins_total; hedges that do not win are load for nothing.

panels.title: Time waiting
panels.description: Goroutine-seconds per second spent between attempts. A rise without a rise in retries per call means Retry-After is being honoured, or the schedule has climbed to its cap.

panels.title: Gets per second, by outcome
panels.description: Every outcome a Get can resolve to. Stacked: the total height is read volume, the degraded and failed bands are what is not being served fresh.

panels.title: Degraded and failed share
panels.description: Degraded: the origin failed but a stale answer was served anyway. Failed: the caller got an error. Degraded sustained means the origin has been down a while; any failed is worth paging on.

panels.title: Fast source errors per second
panels.description: Calls to the fast source that returned an error rather than found=false. Every read is paying the origin's full latency while this is nonzero.

panels.title: Refreshes vs load failures
panels.description: Background refreshes started by ServeAndRefresh: completed successfully, or failed. Sustained load failures with few successful refreshes means the origin cannot keep up with the refresh rate the policy is asking for.

panels.title: In flight vs capacity
panels.description: Requests holding a slot, against the capacity the algorithm currently allows. Riding the capacity line means saturated; a capacity falling away from a flat in-flight is the algorithm deciding the work has got slower.

panels.title: Shed share, by priority
panels.description: Share of inbound requests refused, split by the band that was refused. Stacked: sheddable alone is the package working as intended, any critical means capacity is gone entirely.

panels.title: Wait time vs service time
panels.description: p99 of the queue wait under WithMaxWait, against p99 of how long an admitted request holds its slot. Wait has no observations without WithMaxWait; wait approaching service time means the queue is costing about as much as the work.

panels.title: Requests per second, by priority and result
panels.description: Everything that reached the limiter. Stacked: the total height is inbound volume, the shed bands are what was given up rather than served.
